opportunities.title: SHE ORBITS Summer School 2026
opportunities.description: The SHE ORBITS Summer School is our flagship international educational program, bringing together students, researchers, and professionals from around the world for an immersive nine-week journey through the most exciting fields of space science and engineering. Designed by leading experts, the program combines technical lectures, interactive workshops, research discussions, and collaborative projects to provide participants with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.
opportunities.detail: Designed by leading experts, the Summer School combines technical lectures, interactive workshops, research discussions, and collaborative projects. Curriculum spans orbits, black holes, autonomous spacecraft and AI, space robotics, astronomy and astrophysics, astrobiology and exoplanets, space law and policy, quantum mechanics in space, and multi-body dynamics and control.

Participants will study the effects of microgravity, radiation, isolation, and long-duration missions on human health while learning about astronaut healthcare, biomedical monitoring, countermeasures, and the future of medicine for lunar and Mars exploration.

opportunities.title: Interdisciplinary Spring School
opportunities.description: A five-week multidisciplinary space program combining expert-led learning, technical applications, collaborative projects, and exploration of key space science and engineering disciplines.
opportunities.detail:
The Interdisciplinary Spring School is an intensive five-week multidisciplinary educational experience designed to provide participants with a broad foundation in modern space science and engineering. The program combines theoretical learning with practical applications, expert-led sessions, collaborative activities, and project-based work across multiple disciplines.

Participants explore spacecraft systems, mission architecture, satellite technologies, orbital mechanics, programming and simulation, geospatial intelligence, Earth observation, artificial intelligence, autonomous spacecraft, formation flying, life-support systems, space habitats, electronics, communications, space medicine, and mission design. By bringing these disciplines together within one integrated learning experience, the Spring School helps participants understand how different areas of space science and engineering connect within real missions while preparing them for advanced learning, research, and future careers in the global space sector.


WEEKLY COURSE STRUCTURE & TOPIC DETAILS

WEEK 1 Space Systems & Human Context

Theme: Understanding how space missions are built and who they are built for

Class 1 Introduction to Space Missions & Architecture

Participants are introduced to different types of space missions, including Earth observation, communication, navigation, and exploration missions[cite: 1]. The session explains the space segment, ground segment, and user segment, emphasizing end-to-end mission thinking[cite: 1].

Class 2 Satellite Subsystems & Space Technology

This session explores the major satellite subsystems such as power, thermal control, communication, attitude determination and control, and payload systems[cite: 1]. Real engineering trade-offs are discussed to show how mission requirements shape system design[cite: 1].

Class 3 Programming for Simulation (Absolute Beginners)

Participants learn the basics of programming using Python or MATLAB, focusing on computational thinking, plotting, and simple simulations[cite: 1]. No prior coding experience is required[cite: 1].

Class 4 Humans in Space: Space Biology Foundations

This class introduces how the human body responds to microgravity[cite: 1]. Topics include fluid shifts, muscle and bone changes, and why space biology and medicine are essential for safe human spaceflight[cite: 1].

WEEK 2 Orbits, Earth & Geospatial Intelligence

Theme: How satellites move around Earth and observe our planet

Class 5 Orbital Mechanics (Conceptual & Visual)

Participants learn why satellites orbit Earth, the differences between LEO, MEO, and GEO, and how velocity and energy shape orbital motion, using visual and intuitive explanations[cite: 1].

Class 6 Orbit Propagation & Space Environment

This session covers orbital elements, coordinate frames, and environmental effects such as atmospheric drag and gravitational perturbations, building a foundation for understanding real mission constraints[cite: 1].

Class 7 Orbit Simulation & Ground Track

Participants simulate satellite orbits and visualize ground tracks, learning how orbital motion translates into Earth coverage and geospatial applications[cite: 1].

Class 8 Space Medicine: Microgravity Effects & Countermeasures

This class focuses on health challenges faced by astronauts, including muscle atrophy, bone loss, and radiation exposure, along with countermeasures used on the International Space Station[cite: 1].

WEEK 3 Intelligent Space Systems & Life Support

Theme: Autonomy, coordination, and sustaining life beyond Earth

Class 9 Autonomous & Intelligent Space Systems

Participants explore why autonomy is critical in modern space missions, including rule-based systems, basic AI concepts, and smart satellite constellations[cite: 1].

Class 10 Spacecraft Formation Flying

This focused session introduces multi-satellite missions where spacecraft operate in coordinated formations[cite: 1]. Applications in Earth observation and deep-space missions are discussed conceptually[cite: 1].

Class 11 Life Support Systems & Space Habitats

Participants learn how air, water, and food systems are managed in space, and how closed-loop life support systems enable long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars[cite: 1].

Class 12 Geospatial Intelligence & Space Data Applications

This class connects satellite data to real-world applications such as climate monitoring, disaster response, urban planning, and environmental analysis[cite: 1].

WEEK 4 Space Electronics & Future Human Missions

Theme: From understanding concepts to applying knowledge

Class 13 Space Medicine & Future Human Missions

Participants explore challenges of future Moon and Mars missions, including radiation exposure, psychological health, artificial gravity concepts, and open research questions[cite: 1].

Class 14 Space Electronics & Communication Systems

Participants are introduced to sensors, onboard electronics, and communication systems, understanding how hardware and software work together in space missions[cite: 1].

WEEK 5 Mission Design, Research & Mini Projects

Class 15 Space Mission Design & Research Methodology

This session explains how space missions and research projects are designed, how research questions are framed, and how to read and understand scientific papers[cite: 1].

Class 16 Mini Project Presentations & Mentoring

In the final session, participants present their mini projects and receive feedback and mentoring from the SHE ORBITS team, along with guidance on future learning pathways[cite: 1].

opportunities.title: World Space Week 2025
opportunities.description: A seven-day international SHE ORBITS initiative combining space education, inspiration, technical learning, community engagement, and the official launch of its global community.
opportunities.detail:
Format: Online Campaign · Conference · Workshop · Space Challenge · Community Launch

SHE ORBITS marked World Space Week 2025 with a seven-day international initiative created to officially introduce SHE ORBITS to the world, grow its visibility, and establish its first global community of women passionate about space, STEM, innovation, and exploration.
Rather than limiting the celebration to a single event, SHE ORBITS designed a complete week-long experience combining education, inspiration, interaction, technical learning, and community building.


The 7-Day Journey

Day 1 — Launch Day
SHE ORBITS officially launched its digital presence and opened applications for its upcoming programs. The day introduced the company's mission, vision, and future direction while inviting the first members of the SHE ORBITS community to become part of its journey.

Day 2 — Space Heroes Day
Participants explored the stories of astronauts, scientists, engineers, and pioneers who shaped humanity's journey into space. The day focused particularly on inspiring role models and demonstrating the many different pathways through which people can contribute to the space sector.

Day 3 — Roadmap & Interest Day
SHE ORBITS presented its vision for a structured Space Learning Journey, showing how participants could progress from foundational STEM knowledge to AI, technical projects, research, leadership, and careers in the space industry. An interest form was also introduced to understand the community's interests and future learning needs.

Day 4 — Introductory Conference
The central live event of the week brought together the emerging SHE ORBITS community with speakers and guests from the international space ecosystem. The conference introduced SHE ORBITS in greater depth, explored opportunities in space and STEM, and created an open space for discussion, questions, and connection.

Day 5 — Interactive Workshop
Participants moved from inspiration to hands-on learning through an interactive STEM/space workshop. The experience combined structured educational content with practical activities and technical demonstrations, giving participants an opportunity to engage directly with space-related concepts and tools.

Day 6 — Space Challenge
The community came together for an interactive challenge centered on the question: “What shaped your space journey?” Participants shared a book, project, idea, thought, or theory that influenced their interest in space. The challenge encouraged creativity, personal storytelling, and community interaction, with winners receiving opportunities to participate in future SHE ORBITS programs.

Day 7 — Closing Vision & Community Launch
The week concluded by reflecting on the journey, sharing the program's achievements and community growth, and presenting the future vision of SHE ORBITS. The closing also marked the launch of the SHE ORBITS community space on Discord, creating a continuing environment for connection, learning, collaboration, and future opportunities.


Beyond One Week

World Space Week 2025 was designed not simply as a celebration of space, but as the beginning of a community.

Across seven days, SHE ORBITS moved from launch → inspiration → education → connection → hands-on learning → participation → community, laying the foundation for a long-term ecosystem dedicated to helping women explore opportunities across space and STEM.

World Space Week 2025 became the starting point of the SHE ORBITS journey — bringing together the first community of women ready to learn, build, lead, and shape the future of space.

opportunities.title: SEEC (Space Exploration Educators Conference)
opportunities.description: SHE ORBITS received a fully funded invitation to attend SEEC 2026 in Texas, connecting with NASA professionals, astronauts, educators, researchers, and global space-education leaders.
opportunities.detail:
SHE ORBITS was honored with a fully funded, all-expenses-paid invitation to attend the Space Exploration Educators Conference (SEEC) 2026 in Texas, hosted by Space Center Houston, the official visitor center of NASA’s Johnson Space Center.
Held from February 5–7, 2026, the conference brought together educators, NASA professionals, astronauts, researchers, industry experts, and space-education organizations from around the world.
SHE ORBITS participated in the conference and was represented in the United States, engaging with international leaders across space exploration, STEM education, experiential learning, Earth observation, leadership, and global collaboration. The experience provided valuable strategic insights and opportunities to connect SHE ORBITS’ mission with the broader international space-education ecosystem.
This invitation represented an important recognition of SHE ORBITS’ growing international presence and its work to expand access to space education and opportunities for women from emerging and non-traditional space-faring communities.
Through opportunities such as SEEC, SHE ORBITS continues to build bridges between emerging space communities and the global space industry—creating pathways for the next generation of women to enter, contribute to, and ultimately help shape the future of the space sector.
